name: Bewan
description: an elven ruin on the western coast of Auridon, just southwest of the town of Dawnbreak containing Sea Viper raiders.
loadtext: The high vaulted halls of Bewan were originally built in the Merethic Era as a shrine to Trinimac. Bewan was abandoned early in the First Era when the priesthood moved to the grand Trinimac Chantry outside Skywatch.
summary: Some of the Sea Vipers are acting drunk. Parts of the ruin are flooded with shallow water. Argar's corpse can be found near the delve boss during Ruthless Competition. Rats and snakes are found in numbers within. thumb|Interior of Bewan
related_quests: Lost Bet; Through a Veil Darkly
notable_items: Camandar's Journal; Digging Orders; Warning: I Heard You!
notes: The large southernmost room of the dungeon was added in Update 16 to be used in the quest Through a Veil Darkly. In Update 17, a few Maormer corpses and passive spiders were added.; Despite the number of quests requiring this dungeon, it is possible to actually do them all in one visit, even for Aldmeri Dominion characters, if one juggles one's prologue quests carefully.; This includes finding the Dusk Mushrooms for The Demon Weapon even as a Covenant or Pact character, since they are available in all three delves, so even though the quest has pointed you to a faction-appropriate one, they can be collected here instead if you're at the right stage of the quest.

name: Del's Claim
description: a mine in southern Auridon, just northwest of the city of Vulkhel Guard, containing Veiled Heritance members.
loadtext: No one believed the old ouster Del when he staggered into Vulkhel Guard and claimed he'd found a huge deposit of lapis lazuli in the hills, but it turned out to be true, and now Del's Claim is one of the most profitable mines on Auridon.
summary: The miners were all slain when the heritants moved in. They plan to use it as a secure base of operations.
related_quests: Repentant Son; The Wing of the Indrik

name: Entila's Folly
description: an abandoned mine in central Auridon, just southwest of the city of Skywatch containing spiders and giant wasps.
loadtext: Kinlady Entila of Clan Auralus had a vivid dream that beneath the coastal cliffs near Skywatch was a fabulous fist-sized gem, the Egg of the World. Based on the directions in her vision, she hired a score of miners to dig until they found it. The funds of Clan Auralus ran out first.
summary: thumb|right|The interior of Entila's Folly
notes: The spiders that ambush you by dropping from the ceiling throughout the delve are immune to damage until their descent animation is fully completed.

name: Mehrunes' Spite
description: a Daedric ruin in the northwestern corner of Auridon, just west of the city of Firsthold containing Daedra and Veiled Heritance members.
loadtext: Before the followers of the Prophet Veloth left Summerset for Morrowind, they built several secret shrines for illicit worship of the Daedric Princes. It is believed that after the Chimer left Summerset, all of these heretical shrines were found and destroyed.
summary: Butterflies, frogs and rats are found in numbers within.
related_quests: Take Me Home; Veiled Darkness in Auridon

name: Ondil
description: an Aldmeri ruin in the center of Auridon, just south of the town of Mathiisen containing a local vampire and his minions.
loadtext: Now ruined, the subterranean halls of Ondil were built in the early First Era to house Kinlady Fiorallelle's extensive collection of ceramic figurines. It was abandoned before completion when its alignment with the constellation of the Atronach was found to be seven percent off true.
summary: There is a chest south of the ruins, beside a wall.thumb|right|Ondil's library chamber During the quest Long Lost Lore, a Forgotten Tome can be found here if your character is of the Dominion.
related_quests: Getting the Band Together; Long Lost Lore; Eye of Fate; The Wing of the Indrik

name: Wansalen
description: an Aldmeri ruin in northeastern Auridon, on the western edge of Quendeluun containing Ebonheart Pact soldiers and undead.
location: On the western edge of Quendeluun, near the northeastern shore of Auridon
loadtext: Legend has it that the excavation of Wansalen was halted, and the halls abandoned, when the Elven miners roused and angered an ancient rock-spirit called a Gheatus. But the wise Sapiarchs of the Crystal Tower dismiss this story as a fable with no truth to it.
summary: The tunnels are off limits to the First Auridon Marines as they are prone to collapse. As a result, forces of the Pact have been using the tunnels as a base of operations on Auridon. To reach the skyshard, go straight into the large room with two staircases, follow the watery path south, and head to the corner of the west room between two guards.

name: Burroot Kwama Mine
description: a kwama mine located just west of Elden Root in Grahtwood, containing thunderbugs.
loadtext: Expatriates often try to bring beloved aspects of their culture with them when they emigrate. So it was with Llevyn Buratil of Narsis in Morrowind, who tried to establish a kwama mine in Grahtwood. The experiment was less than a resounding success.
summary: The thunderbugs infesting the mine have killed many of the kwama within. They are led by a massive thunderbug named Stormhead the Ravenous. Some notes can be found here. Scribs are found inside and just outside.

name: Mobar Mine
description: a mine just south of Elden Root in Grahtwood containing bandits.
loadtext: With the flurry of construction going on in nearby Elden Root, the Foriniel Brothers have reopened Mobar Mine to supply the builders with clay for making bricks. Strangely, no one has heard from the Foriniels in over a week.
summary: It was opened to help provide building materials for Elden Root, but no one has heard from the owners in some time. Enslaved Miners can be found within.

name: Ne Salas
description: an Ayleid ruin south of Elden Root and west of Haven in Grahtwood, containing Daggerfall Covenant soldiers.
location: South of Elden Root, west of Haven
loadtext: The Ayleids who fled to Valenwood after the Slave Rebellion were mostly those who worshiped the Daedric Princes, which was outlawed under Empress Alessia. The Slave Queen melded the Aedra worshiped by her human and remaining Elven subjects to create the Eight Divines.
summary: The ruin is connected to Salas En in Alik'r by way of an ancient portal system which forms the basis of two related quests. The portal is not usable. You'll find Cirmo and Aldmeri Dominion forces camped outside the ruin. The containers in the exterior camp, including barrels, crates and a backpack, are all owned. Three dead Wood Elf Laborers are lying in front of the entrance, near a cooking fire. right|thumb|Interior

name: The Scuttle Pit
description: a cave in eastern Grahtwood, north of Haven and east of Elden Root containing spiders.
location: North of Haven and east of Elden Root
loadtext: The spiders of Tamriel are fearsome carnivores that prey on everything they can catch, even each other. They have adapted to every environment, both above and below ground, and there seems to be no limit as to how large they can grow.
summary: Two dead Giant Spiders can be found in the delve: One at the bottom level of the second large room and one behind the Spider Queen.

name: Vinedeath Cave
description: a cave in northeastern Grahtwood, east of Elden Root containing spriggans and stranglers.
loadtext: The strangler is a carnivorous plant that lurks in the shadows of the forest floor. Its tentacles excrete a sticky, sweet substance that attracts prey. The strangler reacts to warmth and movement by lashing out with its tentacles and drawing what it captures into its hungry maw.
summary: The corpse of Storgh, an Orc and Orthelos's friend, can be found in the southeast chamber. A Scrap of Storgh's Journal is located next to his corpse, while the skyshard sits across from it. A chest can spawn near the tunnel leading out west from the room with Storgh's corpse in it, between a large root and the wall. The delve's boss is located in the southwest chamber. A chest can spawn atop a rocky ledge behind the boss, where the fog accumulates near a rack of large ribs.
notes: The cave is mentioned in Garick's Message as a place not suitable as a hideout due to its haunted nature. Reading the note adds a marker to your map for this location.

name: Wormroot Depths
description: an Ayleid ruin in the northwest corner of Grahtwood containing Daedra.
loadtext: Regarded by scholars of the arcane as the apex achievement of the Wild Elves' magical art, the so-called Ayleid Wells are believed to use Aetherial crystal to aggregate magicka from starlight—even in subterranean locations.
summary: They are led by a dremora named Raynia. This delve can be discovered by reading a note at Nazura's Nibbles in the Redfur Trading Post.
related_quests: Ayleid Trinkets in Grahtwood; The Demon Weapon; Light in the Darkness
notes: Archibert Dantaine erroneously states the Worm Cult occupies the ruins. His information is more likely out of date than outright incorrect: it clearly *was* once a Worm Cult lair, because Mannimarco has used it to stash some copies of his records from the interrogation of Sai Sahan. But there are no actual cultists or summoned undead present when the player visits, only Daedra.; Aside from the delve's regular quest (Light in the Darkness), and the Undaunted daily (Ayleid Trinkets in Grahtwood), Aldmeri Dominion characters can be sent here twice by Abnur Tharn, in both the Main Quest (The Tharn Speaks) and the Elsweyr prologue (The Demon Weapon). However, since it is impossible to be on both of these quests simultaneously since being on one of them prevents the other from starting, it is impossible to fulfill all the quest-related visits to this dungeon in a single visit; it must be visited twice. Covenant and Pact characters are unaffected by this, since they are sent elsewhere during the Main Quest.

name: Barrow Trench
description: a mine in northwestern Greenshade, north of Moonhenge containing bandits.
loadtext: Some caverns are prized, not for the ore that can be mined from them, but for the exotic fungus that grows within them. Barrow Trench is the latter sort.
summary: A skyshard is located east of the delve, along the base of the cliff. They are mining ore throughout and are led by Overseer Basri. There is a camp with a cooking fire outside the delve. There is a Delivery Contract at the delve's entrance that grants the related quest. A note lies on the picnic table in the center of the northern chamber. The delve's boss is located atop a wooden platform in the southern side of the southwestern chamber. The delve's skyshard is located outside the one-way exit outside the eastern side of the southwestern chamber. Rats are found in number within.

name: Carac Dena
description: an Ayleid ruin in southern Greenshade, south of the Labyrinth containing ogres.
loadtext: Though abandoned thousands of years ago, many Ayleid ruins are still lit by the blue glowing varla and welkynd stones found in them. These stones are among the so-called "Aetherial Crystals," gems that can store, transform, and emit magicka.
summary: The tribe has recently moved into the ruin and is led by Urrumaz the Terrifying. Fleshflies are found in numbers within.
notes: The ogres with white fur and face paint in the ruins have a much lower health pool compared to the ogres found elsewhere in the game, including the other kind in the ruins, thus they pose little threat.

name: Gurzag's Mine
description: a mine in eastern Greenshade, south of Marbruk containing undead.
loadtext: One of the reasons the Wood Elves tolerate the presence of Orc clans in Valenwood is that the Wood Orcs are nearly as talented at forging metal as their northern cousins. Bosmer who follow the Green Pact still have a use for metal tools and weapons, and buy them from the Orcs.
summary: They are led by the wraith Retribution. The curse in the mine was brought forth due to the nearby Wood Orcs buying an axe from Forthor, who actually applied the curse himself on the axe with the effects of attracting spirits and undead to it. Fleshflies are found in number within.

name: Harridan's Lair
description: a cave in eastern Greenshade, northwest of Marbruk containing senche-tigers.
loadtext: According to the Spinners in Marbruk, these cliffs were once inhabited by a flock of the rare, and possibly extinct, cockatiel harpies. They were said to kidnap young male hunters as mates, thus the saying about the lovestruck, "He's carried off to Harridan's."
summary: The pride that lives in the cave is led by the matriarch, Razorclaw. Torchbugs and an unusually high amount of frogs are found in numbers within.
notes: The Letter from Bashshi-ra, found in Woodhearth, marks this location on your map.; In order to get the achievement, you not only have to kill Razorclaw, but the two Senche-Tigers accompanying her.

name: Naril Nagaia
description: an Ayleid ruin in southwestern Greenshade, east of Woodhearth, containing Veiled Heritance members.
loadtext: These ruins have a bad reputation in nearby Woodhearth—which is not surprising, considering their name in Ayleidoon means "final death."
summary: The heritants cell here is led by Archmage Camaano. A chest can be found on an altar in the westernmost chamber, in the southeastern section of the room. The skyhard can be found in the southwestern chamber. Many Heritance members lay dead in the southern chambers. Mercano's Journal can be found in the southeastern chamber, next to Archmage Camaano. Fleshflies and Spiders are found in numbers within.
related_quests: Culinary Justice in Greenshade; A Friend In Need; The Misuses of Knowledge
notes: The name of the ruin means "final death" in Ayleidoon.

name: The Underroot
description: a cave in western Greenshade, southeast of the Seaside Sanctuary containing lamia.
loadtext: When Valenwood was conquered by Emperor Reman II late in the First Era, the princes of the Camoran Dynasty were exiled and the province was reorganized into nine small, semi-autonomous kingdoms. This bolstered local pride, and made Valenwood easier to govern.
summary: The group is led by Domina Ssaranth. According to a Blood-Spattered Love Note found in the cave, The Underroot was not only used as a trysting spot, but the Lamia were thought to be friendly. Two passive senches are found near the boss' room. Snakes and torchbugs are found in number within.

name: Black Vine Ruins
description: a set of Ayleid ruins in northeastern Malabal Tor, west of the Baandari Trading Post containing Red Sun bandits and stranglers.
location: West of the Baandari Trading Post
loadtext: The name of the long-dead Ayleid clan that built these halls has been forgotten. Their latter-day name is Black Vine, for the writhing, dark vines that spill from the crumbling arches and doorways.
summary: A Blackvine Strangler can be found deep within the ruin. Rats and spiders are found in numbers within. Black Vine Villa lies east of the ruins, and the Silvenar Vale Dolmen lies to the south. thumb|right|In the ruins
related_quests: Brothers and Bandits; The Demon Weapon

name: Dead Man's Drop
description: a mine in eastern Malabal Tor, on the shore east of Fuller's Break containing Ra Gada pirates.
loadtext: Thanks to the Green Pact, the more industrious Wood Orcs of Valenwood have prospered by mining coal and kindlepitch and selling it to the Bosmer, who won't cut down trees for wood to burn, but still need to fire their forges. Dead Man's Drop is one such mine.
summary: They are led by Captain Shammin. Centipedes, rats and spiders are found in numbers within.
related_quests: An Apocalyptic Situation; A Nord in Need
notes: The book Dead Man's Drop, found in the Velyn Harbor Mages Guild, marks this location on your map.

name: Hoarvor Pit
description: a cave in central Malabal Tor, southwest of Vulkwasten containing hostile wildlife.
loadtext: The hoarvor, a colossal, blood-sucking tick, is one of the most repulsive creatures in all of Tamriel. To anyone who knows the Bosmer, it will come as no surprise that many have a perverse admiration for the hoarvor, adopting the gross insect as a sort of mascot.
summary: thumb|right|Inside the pit An ogrim named Oghezai is bound deep within the cave, being fed on by the blood-sucking hoarvors that inhabit it. The hoarvors also feed on dead senche, crocodiles, and Bosmer. A small valley is found in the northern part, infested with crocodiles. Centipedes, lizards, spiders and torchbugs are found in numbers within. A copy of Horrors of the Strid Basin can be found in a tunnel leading to the second floor in the southern portion of the delve. A copy of the Lorebook A Nereid Stole My Husband can be found on the second floor, in the tunnel west of Oghezai's chamber. A note can be found in the round chamber at the western end of this tunnel, where it turns north towards the northernmost chamber. A chest can also be found in this portion of the tunnel. The skyshard can be found in the northernmost chamber. A chest can be found east of the skyshard. Another chest can be found further east, near the mouth of the cave leading into the tunnel heading back towards t
notes: The letter She Dared Me, found in the Dra'bul Chieftain's Longhouse, marks this location on your map.

name: Shael Ruins
description: a haunted Ayleid ruin in southern Malabal Tor, just north of the Grahtwood gate.
loadtext: No one is sure nowadays which of the Daedric Princes were worshiped by the Ayleid clan who built the haunted corridors of Shael, but it was certainly one of the more malefic of the Lords of Oblivion. Specters are the residents that walk its halls.
summary: It can be found south of Abamath. Rats and spiders are found in numbers within.
related_quests: The Spirit Trap in Malabal Tor

name: Tomb of the Apostates
description: a cave in southern Malabal Tor, west of Tanglehaven containing undead.
loadtext: The Green Pact, the Spinners say, contains its own punishment for those who turn their back on it. Such apostates become the Accursed of Y'ffre, doomed to haunt lost corners of the Green until they find a way to redeem themselves.
summary: They are led by a skeletal sorcerer, Gwaeregil. Elorwen's spirit can also be found here, guiding people to her skeleton and family heirloom. thumb|right|Inside the tomb Centipedes, spiders and torchbugs are found in numbers within.
notes: The letter Rogue Elements, found in Deepwoods, marks this location on your map.

name: Claw's Strike
description: a ruined Khajiiti temple in western Reaper's March, north of the Do'Krin Monastery, containing Dawnmead Bandits.
loadtext: Adoption of the Riddle'Thar Epiphany was not without controversy: when the priests of the Shrine of the Consummate S'rendarr in the Jodewood refused to accept the new edicts, they were exiled and the temple deconsecrated. Today it is a bandit lair.
summary: They are led by Fishbreath. This delve contains a Skyshard, three copies of Skooma Runner Logs, and a Note to Marianas. The Shrine of the Golden Eye is located through one of two hidden doors here and must be visited to complete the quest Eye of Fate. Due to being a skooma-manufacturing den, a large number of lootable alchemy bottles are found inside, offering a good source of potions concentrated in one location. Rats and torchbugs are found in numbers within.
related_quests: Eye of Fate; To Honor the Fallen; Mascot Theft in Reaper's March; A Moonlit Shadow

name: Fardir's Folly
description: an Ayleid ruin in northeastern Reaper's March, north of Fort Sphinxmoth containing Colovian raiders.
loadtext: For generations, tomb robbers have been trying to find their way into the halls beneath the Ayleid ruin known locally as Fardir's Folly. Word has reached Dune that they may finally have succeeded.
summary: They are led by Ravo Peltrasius. There are more than a dozen bookshelves in the ruin and an Ayleid Well. Centipedes are found in numbers within.
notes: The northernmost part of the ruins, which is just outside of the zone boundaries, was probably originally supposed to represent the ruin of Silorn (note the distinct cross-shaped layout of the ruin). However, Silorn later made a proper appearance in the West Weald zone.

name: Jode's Light
description: a ruined Khajiiti temple in eastern Reaper's March, west of Dune, containing Rotblood goblins and hostile wildlife.
loadtext: The shrine of Jode's Light just outside Pa'alat was founded by Moon-Bishop Thizzrini in the mid-First Era as a place of safe contemplation for all moon-monks, no matter when they were born on the ja'Kha'jay. It was abandoned during the mass mortality of the Thrassian Plague.
summary: A Khajiit's Lost Journal Page is located on top of a crate at the entrance. Beetles and torchbugs are found in numbers within. The skyshard is located in the northwestern chamber, near the northern wall. Giant Bats inhabit this room. The tunnel to the south leads to the delve's boss. The Second Khajiiti Journal Page is located in the passage leading to the boss. A Third Khajiiti Journal Page is located near the boss room's northern one-way exit.
related_quests: Beyond a Veil of Twilight; The Demon Weapon; The Wing of the Dragon; Test of Faith
notes: The Ja'zennji Siir style is based on the outfits worn by the monks of Jode's Light temple (Ja'zennji Siir is Jode's Light in Ta'agra).

name: Kuna's Delve
description: a mine in northern Reaper's March, south of Arenthia containing trolls.
loadtext: There is a ready market in Senchal and Torval for Khajiiti relics from the glorious period of the Anequine Conquests. Objects that date from the reign of Darloc Brae the Golden Beast are particularly prized.
summary: Wolf, Young Bat loadtext=There is a ready market in Senchal and Torval for Khajiiti relics from the glorious period of the Anequine Conquests. Objects that date from the reign of Darloc Brae the Golden Beast are particularly prized. }} They are led by a massive armored troll known as Limbrender. Centipedes and torchbugs are found in numbers within. Reading Supplies for the Delve at Kuna's office in Rawl'kha will mark this location on your map.

name: Thibaut's Cairn
description: a crypt in central Reaper's March, east of Vinedusk Village containing undead.
loadtext: The cemeteries and graveyards of Reaper's March overflow with the dead slain in war after war, but at least their survivors could always count on them resting quietly. However, that was before Molag Bal began his Planemeld.
summary: thumb|right|The lich's chamberThe Cairn is named for its most noted "guest," the famed Thibault of Kvatch. Thibault was a general of Colovia, and in his time some hundreds of years ago he was one of the anchor points for the Hastrel Cohort. The details of Thibault's death have been lost. Fleshflies and rats are found in numbers inside. Rithlen the traveling merchant can be found walking along the road east of the cairn.
notes: The boss for Thibaut's Cairn was originally found in an outside higher area after going through and exiting the delve. Now the boss is inside and the outside area has one Ghost, one Skeletal Blademaster and one Skeletal Marksman.

name: Weeping Wind Cave
description: a cave in southeastern Reaper's March, northeast of Willowgrove containing werewolves.
loadtext: According to the "Speluncus Tamrielicum," the reason Nirn is seemingly riddled with natural caverns is that, like a living body, the world is veined with a system of nodes and capillaries that once pulsed with the divine essence of the Aedra who created it.
summary: The pack is led by Nimriian. Butterflies, fleshflies and torchbugs are found in numbers within.
related_quests: The Dark Behind the World; A Night to Forget
notes: The generic Wolfpack enemies have a very small chance of turning into a werewolf during combat.

name: Aldunz
description: a Dwemer ruin in the southern Alik'r Desert, east of Bergama containing Dwemer constructs.
loadtext: Though some Dwarven automatons were clearly designed for defense of the facilities in which they're found, the function of other constructs is less clear. Some appear to be tasked with maintaining other machines, lubricating joints and replacing worn-out parts.
summary: Dwarven Sphere, Dwarven Spider, Flame Atronach, Swarming Dwarven Spider loadtext=Though some Dwarven automatons were clearly designed for defense of the facilities in which they're found, the function of other constructs is less clear. Some appear to be tasked with maintaining other machines, lubricating joints and replacing worn-out parts. loadscreen=ON-load-Dwemer 01.jpg }}Scorpions are found in numbers within. Hazards include lava pools.
related_quests: Molten Pearls of Alik'r Desert; The Precursor; Tharayya's Trail
notes: This is one of the locations where the Precursor Dummy parts resides

name: Coldrock Diggings
description: a mine in the northern Alik'r Desert, southeast of Tava's Blessing containing vampires.
loadtext: The shipwrights at nearby Tava's Blessing depend upon the mine at Coldrock for grit-rock, used in sanding wooden planks, and holystone, a light pumice used for cleaning the decks.
summary: The mine produced grit-rock and holystone for shipwrights at Tava's Blessing before being abandoned. Young Bats swarm from Bat Hollows in the northeastern tunnels. Dead Merchants and Captive Withered Hands, victims of the vampires, can be found inside. Scorpions are found in numbers within.

name: Divad's Chagrin Mine
description: a mine in central Alik'r Desert, southeast of Sentinel containing Sandgrubber goblins.
loadtext: "Divad's Chagrin" is an epic poem of the Redguards describing the great hero's remorse at forsaking the life of a musician to fight tyranny and injustice. No one seems to know what the story of Divad has to do with this shallow mine in the desert.
summary: Beetles, lizards and rats are found in numbers within. Sorhab and his goat are located near the wayshrine. The Lost Caravan lies south of the mine, and Tu'whacca's Throne is to the north. Several dead Dunmer are located in the tunnel near the entrance. A note on top of a stack of crates explains that the goblins in the mine were laborers in the mine, and that no one wanted to buy them. The mine's overseers had gone missing. The Dunmer corpses presumably belong to the people who owned the goblins. A chest can spawn near this stack of crates. The western chamber contains a camp with cots located beneath tarps. There is a dining table further south, and Dunmer corpses are everywhere. Some of them are laying on cots, and may have been killed as they slept. A shield is propped up by a greatsword over a circle of bones, which lies beneath a small tree to the south. Armin is located here A note is located atop a pile of crates near a Dunmer corpse in the southern chamber. The note is located
related_quests: The Search is Over; The Towers' Fall
notes: All Alik'r Desert delves were enlarged with Update 5. For Divad's Chagrin Mine, the eastern part was added and the middle part was opened to no longer be one-way. The Sandgrubber Butchers, Sandgrubber Hunters and Sandgrubber Savages were deleted, and Durzogs, Even Bigger, Ogres, Sandgrubber Deadeyes and Sandgrubber Fire Mages were added. The Sandgrubber Shaman was present in both. Finally Armin was located at the southern dead end (which now links the middle and eastern parts).

name: Sandblown Mine
description: a depleted copper mine in the southeastern Alik'r Desert, east of HoonDing's Watch containing Khajiit bandits.
loadtext: "Sandblown? Ah, now I recall it—the played-out copper mine south of Kozanset. That pit hasn't been worked since the reign of King Ramzi."
summary: It is inhabited by Khajiit bandits, who feed unwary travelers to the giant snake Huzal. Beetles and snakes are found in numbers within. Unique "Spider Nests" are present on top of bandit bodies in the southwest room. Multiple Young Spiders erupt from it upon approaching and when they are all defeated, you can loot the Spider Nest for a random item, ranging from leveled equipement to Decorative Wax

name: Santaki
description: a Dwemer ruin in the western Alik'r Desert, south of Sentinel containing bandits and Dwemer constructs.
loadtext: When the Rourken Dwemer migrated west to Hammerfell, they found a land rich in untapped mineral wealth. They roamed far from their city of Volenfell in pursuit of it, building deep mines and busy workshops. Many of these sites remain virtually untouched.
summary: Bandit Archer, Bandit Charger, Bandit Marauder, Bandit Skirmisher, Dwarven Sphere, Swarming Dwarven Spider alliance=Daggerfall Covenant zone=Alik'r Desert subzone=Myrkwasa location=South of Sentinel marker_id=Delve loadscreen=ON-load-Dwemer 02.jpg loadtext=When the Rourken Dwemer migrated west to Hammerfell, they found a land rich in untapped mineral wealth. They roamed far from their city of Volenfell in pursuit of it, building deep mines and busy workshops. Many of these sites remain virtually untouched. }}Lizards and scorpions are found in numbers within.

name: Yldzuun
description: a Dwemer ruin in the southeastern Alik'r Desert, southeast of Kozanset containing Imperial soldiers and Dwemer constructs.
loadtext: The scholar Guylaine Marilie asserts that "Yldzuun" can be accurately translated as "Mechanized Paradise." However, Thelwe Ghelein says the name is best rendered as "Steam Closet."
summary: Dwarven Sphere, Dwarven Spider, Imperial Duelist, Imperial Knight, Imperial Marksman, Imperial Soldier, Imperial Pyromancer, Swarming Dwarven Spider alliance=Daggerfall Covenant zone=Alik'r Desert subzone=Tigonus location=Southeast of Kozanset marker_id=Delve loadscreen=ON-load-Dwemer 02.jpg loadtext=The scholar Guylaine Marilie asserts that "Yldzuun" can be accurately translated as "Mechanized Paradise." However, Thelwe Ghelein says the name is best rendered as "Steam Closet." }} The Imperials were hired by Quintus Verres to stop his ex-wife, Tharayya. Rats and scorpions are found in numbers within. Imperials and Dwarven constructs can be found fighting against each other in the western room, which is near the entrance. The western chamber has three sections: the northern section, the center, and the southern section. The north and south lead out to tunnels into other sections of the ruin. A heavy sack is in the southeastern corner of the northern section of the room. A chest lies alo

name: Crypt of the Exiles
description: a tomb in central Bangkorai, south of the Pelin Graveyard containing undead.
loadtext: After High Rock joined the First Empire in 1E 1029, the King of Evermore had a vast cemetery built outside the city to house himself and his descendants, naming it after Saint Pelin of Bangkorai Pass. Some of the empty mausoleums ended up put to other uses than burial.
summary: Fleshflies and rats are found in numbers within.
related_quests: Ancient Armaments in Bangkorai; A Favor Between Kings; The Ravenwatch Inquiry
notes: Prior to a very early update, this delve contained instead Forgotten Assassins, Forgotten Guardians, Forgotten Knights and Forgotten Mystics

name: Klathzgar
description: a Dwemer ruin in southeastern Bangkorai, east of Hallin's Stand and south of the Bangkorai Garrison.
location: East of Hallin's Stand, south of the Bangkorai Garrison
loadtext: The location of the Dwarven ruin called Klathzgar had been lost since the middle of the First Era, when its entrance was hidden by drifting sand. Now the same desert wind that covered it has uncovered it, and its entrance is revealed.
summary: An Altmeri scholar named Pelorrah has been studying these ruins.

name: Rubble Butte
description: an Ayleid ruin in western Bangkorai, north of Hallin's Stand containing Disloyal Nobles and their minions.
loadtext: This underground site is part of Nilata, one of the most extensive Ayleid ruin complexes in Hammerfell. It was occupied by the Wild Elves for at least a thousand years, and its welkynd stones will probably continue to glow for at least another thousand.
related_quests: Back in Time; The Missing Prophecy

name: Torog's Spite
description: an old iron mine in northwestern Bangkorai, northwest of Evermore, containing infighting Agluk Clan and Morkul Clan raiders.
loadtext: This mine once eked out iron ore to its diligent Breton miners, but it has long since been given up to Orcish raiders from Wrothgar.
summary: Its Breton miners were driven out long ago by Orcish invaders from Wrothgar. A Letter from Historian Maaga‎‎ can be read to begin the quest associated with this delve. Deeper into the mine Borzugh's Letter and Thorzhul's Letter can also be found.
notes: The delve was inhabited by Orc raiders (Torog's Spite Archer; Torog's Spite Marauder; Torog's Spite Ravager; Torog's Spite Savage) prior to Patch 1.4.5, having been replaced by Orc clans.; It is named after Torug gro-Igron.

name: Troll's Toothpick
description: a cave in northeastern Bangkorai, north of Kerbol's Hollow containing trolls and bandits.
loadtext: The Knahaten Flu swept through the Mournoth Dungeons, killing everyone, prisoners, guards, and warden alike. The prison was decommissioned and left to decay. Now the locals call it by a different name.

name: Viridian Watch
description: a fort in eastern Bangkorai, northeast of the Bangkorai Garrison containing Bjoulsae Boys bandits.
loadtext: In the early First Era, during the days when the Direnni Hegemony ruled High Rock, a series of watch towers was built along the border with the Reach and Skyrim. Today most of them are nothing more than crumbling ruins.
summary: A chest can be found around the corner from the trapdoor leading into the delve. A heavy sack is located in the hallway west of the entrance, at the corner between the eastern and southern passageways. Quickpaw of Martyr's Crossing can mark this delve on your map. Captured Bretons can be found here. A chest and heavy sack are located west of the boss, in the eastern chamber. Curnard's Journal can be found on a table east of the boss. The Bjoulsae Boys Charter can be found in the delve as well, along with another document. A copy of A Royal Embarrassment can also be found here.

name: Cryptwatch Fort
description: a fort just north of the Crosswych Wayshrine in Glenumbra containing Bloodthorn cultists and Red Rook bandits.
loadtext: As the name implies, Cryptwatch Fort was once an underground mausoleum. It was later fortified by the addition of a tower during one of High Rock's many internal conflicts.
summary: Argar's corpse can be found near the delve boss during Ruthless Competition. Rats and torchbugs are found in numbers within.
related_quests: Fortune in Failure; Ache For Cake

name: Enduum
description: an Ayleid ruin on the shore west of Camlorn in Glenumbra containing Aldmeri Dominion soldiers and skeletons.
loadtext: The halls of lost Enduum are given a wide berth by the local Bretons, who claim that its corridors and chambers are haunted by ghosts of the ancient Ayleids who built them back in the .
summary: . }} Rats and spiders and are found in ample numbers within with a squirrel. During the Elsweyr Chapter prologue quest, Daggerfall Covenant characters will be sent here by Abnur Tharn to collect dusk mushrooms for Dagaril-dro.
notes: The Dawn Era reference was [https://www.imperial-library.info/content/lawrence-schick-and-phrastus-altmer-culture noted] to be an error by Lawrence Schick, and is instead intended to be First Era.

name: Ilessan Tower
description: a ruin just west of the Baelborne Rock Wayshrine and east of Daggerfall in Glenumbra containing Red Rook bandits.
location: West of the Baelborne Rock Wayshrine
loadtext: This long abandoned, crumbling tower appears to be an old outwork of the Daggerfall defenses.
summary: This delve can be split into two sections, there are the tower ruins on the western side of the map. Here the Rooks have dispatched an exploration team to loot the tower, led by a powerful storm mage named Gaetane. Rats are found in ample numbers within the tower. In the northeast area of the map is an outdoor area filled with harpies and their nests. The Red Rooks and Harpies have been fighting each other, with casualties on both sides. During "Three Thieves in Daggerfall", you will get access to the Lower Dungeon, an area below the main delve.
related_quests: Red Rook Resources; Red Rook Ransack in Glenumbra; Royal Revelry; Things Lost, Things Found; Three Thieves in Daggerfall

name: Mines of Khuras
description: located on the shore east of Aldcroft, in Glenumbra, and contain Bloodthorn cultists.
loadtext: These extensive mines, once famous as a source of crystals and gems, were abandoned after a ceiling collapse in 1E 2906 rendered most of the tunnels inaccessible.
summary: Peasants have been enslaved by the cult and forced to mine. Rats are found in ample numbers within the tunnels. A heavy sack is located near the end of the tunnel connecting the central chamber to the entrance. Bloodthorn Orders are located in this same tunnel, closer to the delve's entrance. The delve's boss is located in the north central chamber at the end of a dock where there is a pick embedded in stone.
related_quests: A Brush With Death; Through a Veil Darkly
notes: The Mines of Khuras appeared in Arena.; The small tunnel to the northeastern chamber is only open to find Oracle Marieve during the quest Through a Veil Darkly. Enter it on the east side of the east "finger" of the lake where Lilou is.

name: Silumm
description: an Ayleid ruin just north of Daggerfall in Glenumbra containing Aldmeri Dominion soldiers and werewolves.
loadtext: The ruins of Silumm are the westernmost known Ayleid settlement in Tamriel. Abandoned early in the First Era, Silumm was occupied again during the brief height of the Direnni Hegemony, before being left once more to the erosion of time.
summary: thumb|right|Interior Rats are found in ample numbers within. During the quest Long Lost Lore, a Forgotten Tome can be found here if your character is of the Dominion.
related_quests: An Apocalyptic Situation; Long Lost Lore; Royal Revelry

name: Crestshade Mine
description: a mine in central Rivenspire, northwest of Shornhelm containing trolls.
loadtext: This mine is responsible for much of Crestshade's prosperity, but work was suspended when trouble came to the nearby village.
summary: The mine was responsible for most of Crestshade's prosperity, but was closed down when trouble came to the village. It has since been overrun by trolls. Bitterhand Brutes, Bitterhand Menders, Bitterhand Rogues, Bitterhand Scouts and Skeevers are found near the entrance. Fleshflies and rats are found in numbers within.

name: Erokii Ruins
description: Ayleid ruins in northern Rivenspire, northeast of The Doomcrag containing Montclair soldiers.
loadtext: The crumbling walls, arches, and tunnels in Shrouded Pass are all that is left of Erokii, once the greatest Ayleid city in northwest Tamriel. Its destruction occurred so far in the past that no one today knows the date of its downfall.
summary: Rats and torchbugs are found in numbers within.

name: Flyleaf Catacombs
description: tombs in southwestern Rivenspire, southwest of Crestshade containing Bitterhand Bandits.
loadtext: There are at least three kinds of undead in Tamriel: the reanimated, which includes skeletons and zombies; the returned, which includes ghosts and wraiths; and the accursed, which includes vampires and their ilk.
summary: Fleshflies and rats are found in numbers within.

name: Hildune's Secret Refuge
summary: Hildune's Secret Refuge may refer to: *Hildune's Secret Refuge (place), a public dungeon in Rivenspire *Hildune's Secret Refuge (note), a note regarding that dungeon

name: Orc's Finger Ruins
description: Ayleid ruins in eastern Rivenspire, northeast of Fell's Run containing Bitterhand Bandits.
loadtext: "Do not dally, do not linger, in the tomb they call Orc's Finger." —Northpoint Children's Chant
summary: Teeba-Ja can be found held captive inside. Rats are found in numbers within.
related_quests: Darkness Blooms in Rivenspire; A Friend In Need; The Lady's Keepsake; Shedding the Past

name: Tribulation Crypt
description: a tomb in southeastern Rivenspire, east of Hoarfrost Downs containing skeletons.
loadtext: Tribulation Crypt has long been the preferred cemetery of the Rivenspire nobility. Or it was, until the dead began rising from their graves.
summary: It is the preferred cemetery of the Rivenspire nobility. The Legend of Dame Marcelle can be found in the last room of the crypt. The spirit of Marcelle Stenric can be encountered inside, where she will guide you. Centipedes and fleshflies are found in numbers within.

name: Bearclaw Mine
description: a mine on the far east of Stormhaven, north-northwest of the Weeping Giant Wayshrine containing bandits.
location: North-northwest of the Weeping Giant Wayshrine
loadtext: In many parts of Tamriel, black bears are smaller than their brown or white cousins. Not so the black bears of High Rock, which are among the largest seen anywhere.
summary: An unfinished letter can be found at the entrance to the mine. Followers of Vaermina seem to have an interest of the mine, according to the orders found deeper inside the cave. A partly destroyed book and a final note can be found farther in the cave, telling about the sad fate of a miner's family. Killing bandits will sometimes free peasant miners. Beetles and rats are found in numbers within.

name: Farangel's Delve
description: a mine on the southern shore of Stormhaven, west of Farangel's Landing containing Midnight Union smugglers.
loadtext: Who excavated Farangel's Delve, and why, is unknown. What is known is that it was used as a smugglers' den for untold generations, until recently cleaned out and closed by the Lion Guard. However, rumor says it's been reopened….
summary: They are led by Dimitri. It was used as a smuggler's den for generations until it was cleared out and closed by the Lion Guard. Beetles and rats are found in numbers within.

name: Koeglin Mine
description: a mine on the southwest shore of Stormhaven, southeast of Koeglin Village containing Ember-Eye Slavers.
loadtext: Rumor has it this old, shuttered ebony mine has recently been reopened by agents of the Mages Guild.
summary: They are forcing Enslaved Villagers to work the old mines. Beetles, rats and snakes are found within.

name: Norvulk Ruins
description: an Ayleid ruin in the north of Stormhaven, north of Wind Keep containing Dremora.
loadtext: It's unknown what these vaults were called by the Ayleids who built them. They acquired their current name when they were occupied during the Second Empire by the eccentric wizard Norvulk Tome-Hoarder.
summary: Several texts dedicated to Vaermina can be found within the ruins: In Dreams We Awaken is near the entrance to the ruins and Dream of a Thousand Dreamers can be found in the northern part of the large open area. Just before entering that area, you can also read some orders for the followers of Vaermina. Lastly, Dreamers Our Time Has Come is found near the delve's boss, Nariam. Beetles and rats are found in numbers within.
related_quests: Cursed Baubles of Stormhaven; Word from the Dead
notes: Escamel Vette in Wind Keep can mark Norvulk Ruins on your map if you have not yet discovered it.

name: Pariah Catacombs
description: a tomb just south of Pariah Abbey in Stormhaven containing Stonechewer goblins.
loadtext: Once the favored burial site of the elite of Stormhaven, the Menevia Catacombs were abandoned, along with Menevia Abbey, after the Ghost Harrowing of 2E 307. The vaults were renamed the Pariah Catacombs when the Spirit Wardens re-opened the nearby chapel as Pariah Abbey.
summary: Originally called Menevia Catacombs, the tomb was the favored burial place for the elite of Stormhaven, but was abandoned along with Menevia Abbey following the Ghost Harrowing of 2E 307. Beetles and rats are found in numbers within.

name: Portdun Watch
description: a ruin just west of Firebrand Keep in Stormhaven containing bandits.
loadtext: An abandoned outwork of Firebrand Keep, this tower once guarded the crossroads between Wayrest and Alcaire.
summary: Several Captured Knights from the nearby fort can be found inside. Beetles, rats and snakes are found within.

name: The Corpse Garden
description: a crypt in eastern Deshaan, north of the Tal'Deic Fortress containing skeletons.
loadtext: The Siltreen Sanitary Mortuary acquired its ominous new name after it was stricken by an outbreak of undeath. No one is certain why the dead within have chosen to rise and walk among the living.
summary: Fleshflies and rats reside within.
related_quests: Ancestor Wards in Deshaan; Digging Up the Garden

name: Knife Ear Grotto
description: a Daedric ruin in eastern Deshaan, northeast of the town of Silent Mire containing Daedra.
loadtext: Once this place was a shrine to Boethiah known as the Gauntlet Tabernacle, a place where Chimer sailors would stop to pay their respects before sailing overseas. Now it is rumored to be dedicated to other Daedra: the Four Corners of the House of Troubles.
summary: A chest can be found under the stairs in the first large chamber. Rats are found in numbers within.
notes: The dungeon originally contained a statue of Boethiah, which has since been removed.

name: Lady Llarel's Shelter
description: a kwama mine in western Deshaan, just northeast of the town of Narsis.
loadtext: The origins of this cave's name are obscure, but whoever Lady Llarel was it seems unlikely she'd find shelter here now, as the grotto seems to be occupied by a hive of wild kwama.
summary: A dead Dark Elf and a note can be found near the entrance. You have no choice but to head west to traverse the tunnels. A chest can be found beside the wall near the first cluster of kwama eggs on the right at the mouth of the western chamber. Lady Llarel's Journal is beneath a large root on the north side of this chamber. A Kwama Warrior walks among a nest of eggs near the journal. If you kill the warrior, three Kwama Scribs will emerge from the soil. The boss can be found in the southwest corner of the southern chamber, and the skyshard is located north of her. If you're on the delve's quest, you'll find a Bag of Kwama Eggs beside a standing torch near the boss.
related_quests: You Have to Break a Few

name: Lower Bthanual
description: a Dwemer ruin in central Deshaan, containing Dwemer constructs.
loadtext: The brazen doors of this Dwarven site slide open smoothly and without hesitation, mute testimony to the uncanny skill of the Dwemeri engineers who built them ages ago. Perhaps the rest of the site will be in good repair as well.
summary: It is located just north of the monastery at Muth Gnaar. Two books can be found here: the lorebook Dwemer Dreams can be found in the boss chamber, and a copy of War of Two Houses can be found on a table outside. Centipedes and rats are found in numbers within. The is found on an anvil in the southwest corner of the north room.
notes: Swarming Dwarven Spiders in Lower Bthanual were called "Dwemer Spider Swarm‎" when ESO released, but they were quickly renamed properly.

name: Taleon's Crag
description: a cave in southern Deshaan, just south of the Vale of the Ghost Snake, containing kwama.
location: South of the Vale of the Ghost Snake
loadtext: Some have speculated that this site comes by its name because this is where the famous Nord author Taleon Mythmaker chose to retire after his bitter literary feud with Helgreir Lute-Voice. Phrastus of Elinhir, however, regards this theory as "fanciful twaddle."
summary: Scribs and torchbugs are found in numbers inside.
notes: This dungeon was invaded by the Worm Cult during the Battle for the Writhing Wall event.

name: Triple Circle Mine
description: a mine in central Deshaan, just west of the town of Selfora, containing kagouti.
loadtext: Everyone knows the Triple Circle Mine produces the highest quality iron ore in Deshaan. Strange to find such an active mine looking so deserted.
summary: Hlenir Redoran can be found dead inside the mine. Rats are found in numbers within.

name: The Bastard's Tomb
description: an ancient Nordic tomb in southeastern Eastmarch, north-northeast of the Rift gate containing draugr and Stormfist soldiers.
loadtext: This worn-out old copper and turquoise mine has an evil reputation among the locals of southern Eastmarch, though no one will explain exactly why they feel they must avoid it. Perhaps the true reason has been lost, leaving only a general dread.
summary: The soldiers are led by Agnenor the Blade.

name: The Chill Hollow
description: a cave in northeastern Eastmarch, east of Windhelm containing wispmothers and atronachs.
loadtext: The long-lost Snow Elves that once inhabited Skyrim were reputedly immune to cold and could live comfortably in ice caverns. They are said to have bred a species of snow-cedar so hardy it can live even within the heart of a glacier.
summary: It is inhabited by the frost atronach Nomeg Chal. Dead Worm Cultists can be found in the deepest room of the cave, hinting at the source of the out-of-place atronachs roaming the lower tunnels. A chest can spawn in the southernmost end of the central chamber, close to the eastern tunnel. thumb|right|The snow-cedar

name: The Frigid Grotto
description: a cave in southwestern Eastmarch, northwest of Fort Amol containing wildlife.
loadtext: Morachellis Hag-Husband speculated that a troll's third eye was used to view, not the mundane world, but the overworld of spirits coterminous with our own. However, Morachellis also believed that horkers grew into mammoths, and that fire could be classed as a beverage.
summary: Bear, Skeever loadtext=Morachellis Hag-Husband speculated that a troll's third eye was used to view, not the mundane world, but the overworld of spirits coterminous with our own. However, Morachellis also believed that horkers grew into mammoths, and that fire could be classed as a beverage. }}thumb|right|In the grotto Rats and torchbugs are found within.

name: Icehammer's Vault
description: an ancient Nordic tomb in eastern Eastmarch, north of Cragwallow containing draugr.
loadtext: The Icehammers were a famous clan of warriors who fought long and well during the reign of Hoag Merkiller—so well that King Hoag made the head of the clan one of his thanes. But the clan fell on evil times thereafter, and the Icehammer name died out in the last quarter of the First Era.
summary: In addition to being occupied by draugr, undead wolves called Draugulfs can be found in the crypt. A letter from Uggissar to his cousin can be found not far from the entrance. Farther in lies a book about Thane Icehammer. In the northwestern room there is a torn book shedding some more light into the fate of Uggissar and his family who had been hiding in the tomb. In the northern tunnel you can find another note from Uggissar.
related_quests: Dear Cousins; Dragon Lore: Icehammer's Vault

name: Old Sord's Cave
description: a cave in southern Eastmarch, south of Wittestadr containing Stormfist soldiers.
loadtext: Sord Pot-Helm was a prospector who is said to have singlehandedly dug out the cave that bears his name, working until he died at the age of 103, still convinced that just a bit more digging would reveal a fabulous ebony lode.
summary: They are led by Braxek, Eorim the Hammer and Gadof.
notes: Before being removed in a very early update, Bandit Shamans and Bandit Warriors could be found here. They were replaced by Stormfist Shamans and Stormfist Warriors between the July 8th and December 22nd, 2014.

name: Stormcrag Crypt
description: an ancient Nordic tomb in southeastern Eastmarch, south of Jorunn's Stand containing draugr.
loadtext: Grunilda Stormcrag was one of the original Five Hundred Companions who landed on the shores of Skyrim with Ysgramor. After the Snow Elves were defeated, she established her clan holdings on the northern slopes of the Icewind Peaks.
summary: Rats and torchbugs are found in numbers within. Hazards include: Flame Walls. There are more than a dozen bookshelves in the crypt. The Deathknight Stormcrag can be found in the northeastern chamber.

name: Avanchnzel
description: a Dwemer ruin in the southern Rift, south of Honrich Tower, containing dwarven automatons.
loadtext: Based on what little is known about the Dwarven ruin of Avanchnzel, some scholars of Dwemer architecture believe it must be the outer chambers of a much larger site, access to which is now blocked. The automatons defending the place make it too dangerous to inquire further.
summary: There are several bookshelves in the ruin, as well as a lorebook . A Skyshard can be found in the southwestern chamber, while Thzallek Eft occupies the south hall. Centipedes and spiders are found in numbers within. There is a dead Dunmer named Solvar in front of the ruin. If you head through the crevice north of his corpse, you'll find another skyshard, which is guarded by a sleeping bear. A chest can spawn just east of this skyshard.
related_quests: Dead Weight; Into the Outside; The Precursor
notes: Avanchnzel also appeared in Skyrim.

name: Broken Helm Hollow
description: a small cave in the southeastern Rift, east of Forelhost containing wildlife.
loadtext: Bandits from Broken Helm Hollow have long preyed on the road from Riften to Fort Virak in Morrowind. The Riften Guard clears the place out every few seasons, but the bandits always seem to return.
summary: The troll Skullcrusher can be found in the southern chamber.
related_quests: A Diamond in the Root; The Wing of the Gryphon
notes: Broken Helm Hollow also appeared in Skyrim.

name: Faldar's Tooth
description: a ruined fort in the central Rift, east of Honrich Tower containing Darkling cultists.
loadtext: Sacked over a century ago by raiding Orcs from Yashnag's Kingdom, the fort known as Faldar's Tooth has been left to decay ever since by the Jarls of Riften, who have had no need, or no funds, to rebuild it.
summary: A thieves trove can be found beneath a broken crate on the road leading towards the fort, at the round, U-shaped bend in the road. A functioning cooking fire can be found in the center of the exterior courtyard. There is a single piece of poultry that counts as stolen when you take it. It can be found in the southern tower in the courtyard. Some Speech Notes can be found on a table in front of the entrance to the delve's interior. These notes detail how the Darklings are building a shrine to Nocturnal within the ruins. A copy of the lore book, Song of the Askelde Men, can be found near a non-functioning cooking fire in the western portion of the first large chamber inside the delve. The delve's skyshard can be found in the western tunnels, just south of the entrance chamber. Israk Ice-Storm can be found in the chamber just west of the skyshard, trapped in a cell. Speaking with him starts the delve's related quest. The delve's boss, Rozelun, can be found in the southernmost chamber. The
related_quests: Beneath the Surface; The Missing Prophecy; Returning Winter's Bite (does not require entering the delve itself, only the outer grounds); The Wing of the Gryphon
notes: Faldar's Tooth also appeared in Skyrim.

name: Fort Greenwall
description: a fort in the eastern Rift, north of Riften containing bandits.
loadtext: Fort Greenwall was built to guard the road between Riften and Windhelm, but it was sacked by the Akaviri army during the recent invasion, and has yet to be refurbished and regarrisoned by the Ebonheart Pact.
summary: Uggurek the Vile can be found in the large chamber in the southern part of the fort.
related_quests: Breaches of Frost and Fire; Drink, Drink, and Be Merry; Finding Winter's Hammer (does not require entering the delve, only the external grounds)
notes: Fort Greenwall also appeared in Skyrim.

name: Snapleg Cave
description: a cave in the northern Rift, far north-northeast of Nimalten containing bandits.
loadtext: The regulars at the Horker's Tusk in Ivarstead all agree that trouble has taken up residence in Snapleg Cave, but the nature of that trouble is a matter of dispute. Is it bandits? Smugglers? Hagravens? Cultists? The debate rages on.
notes: Snapleg Cave also appeared in Skyrim.

name: Atanaz Ruins
description: Ancient Argonian ruins in eastern Shadowfen, east of Alten Corimont containing a tribe of ruthless Argonian warriors.
loadtext: Those who call the Argonians "primitives" would do well to consider the permanence and elegance of their stonework, built for eternity despite the relentless Black Marsh rot. The still-solid corridors of ancient Atanaz are an instructive example.
summary: The tribe raids other villages, steals their valuables and kills the inhabitants. They also worship a wamasu, which resides deep within the ruins. A guide to caring for this wamasu can be found near the beast. An old Orc's journal can be found next to his corpse. The ruins are home to two species of unique plants with healing properties. A copy of the lore book Sithis can be found next to the delve's entrance. A herd of kagouti and plenty of giant wasps live on the hillside leading up towards the ruin.
related_quests: Give and Take in Shadowfen; Strength of the Father

name: Broken Tusk
description: a Daedric ruin in eastern Shadowfen, north-northeast of the Forsaken Hamlet, containing Daedra.
loadtext: None know today what lost cult of Daedra worshipers built the original shrine in these caverns, nor what they called it. But the lair the Argonians call Broken Tusk exudes an almost palpable sense of the evil that's been done there over the ages.
summary: The shrine contains a number of dead Molag Bal Cultists, who were summoning Daedra to control and release upon the world in the name of Molag Bal, but were quickly overwhelmed. A dying priest of Arkay and a cursed urn can be found deep within the shrine. A book of rituals can be found in the hallway leading to Naeraizozan's chamber. A chest can be found in this hallway as well. Another chest can be found in the northwest corner of Naeraizozan's room. Four banners depicting the emblem of Sheogorath can be found in the hallway beyond the entrance, and a single banner depicting Hircine can be found in the first large chamber. A copy of Ruminations on the Elder Scrolls can be found south from the ruins, across the river. A Thieves Trove is hiding on the other side of the river, beneath a fern just up the slope towards Camp Merciful Reduction. Two crocodiles, a giant wasp and a guar loiter just outside the entrance to the ruins. Rats and Spiders are found in numbers within.
related_quests: Dim and Distant Pasts; Will of the Broken
notes: Broken Tusk Ritual Notes, located at a camp north of Bogmother, will mark Broken Tusk's location on your map if you haven't discovered it already.

name: Chid-Moska Ruins
description: ancient Argonian ruins in southwestern Shadowfen, west of Murkwater containing Blackguards.
loadtext: Argonian scholars are uncertain whether the Chid-Moska xanmeer should be considered part of the larger Xal Ithix complex, or if it is a separate site built by an even more ancient tribe of Lizard-Folk.
summary: thumb|right|Interior
related_quests: Catch the Lightning; Ruthless Competition; A Friend In Need
notes: The delve was inhabited by Outlaws (Outlaw Berserker; Outlaw Bruiser; Outlaw Recruit; Outlaw Sharpshooter) prior to Update 19, having been replaced by Blackguards.

name: Gandranen Ruins
description: an Ayleid ruin in central Shadowfen, southwest of the Hatching Pools containing Ayleid mummies.
loadtext: Tales say that Gandranen was built by an Ayleid sorcerer, a worshiper of Hermaeus Mora who so loved books that she created a series of magical halls that would attract books from across Tamriel, no matter where—or when—they were published.
summary: The Ayleid Fenlords, practitioners of necromancy, made the halls the place where they would go on to live in undeath. The bodies of some Blackguards can also be found here, along with their map piece. The exterior of the delve is surrounded by wasps and swarming wasps. Inside the delve you will meet Zahra, a Khajiit treasure hunter, who needs your help retrieving an Ayleid artifact. A fragment of a note can be found west from the delve's entrance. Parts of an Argonian journal can be found in the northern part of the last room. There is a skyshard located rather close to the entrance, just outside the one-way exit from the delve's last room.
related_quests: Riches Beyond Measure; The Cursed Skull

name: Onkobra Kwama Mine
description: a kwama mine in southeastern Shadowfen, south of Alten Corimont.
loadtext: When the Dark Elves freed their Argonian slaves, some of the Lizard-Folk assumed control of the Dunmeri ventures where they had been laboring in bondage. Not all these ventures have been successful.

name: Shrine of the Black Maw
description: an Ayleid ruin in northwestern Shadowfen, west-northwest of Stormhold containing vampires.
loadtext: Since the inking of the Ebonheart Pact, the trade in enslaved Argonians has been outlawed … but it has not been eradicated. The slavers have merely gone underground—literally, in the case of those using the Ayleid halls of Varakun as their lair.
summary: The ruin was once known as Varakun, and was a base for illegal slavers. Recently, however, a group of vampires led by a former slave named Peers-Through-Glass have entered the ruin, killing all the slavers. A Free Argonian's Manifesto can be found near here. Other notable items here include a Skyshard and an Ayleid Well. Rats and spiders are found in numbers within.

name: Emberflint Mine
description: a mine in central Stonefalls, southeast of Ebonheart containing Stonefire Cultists.
loadtext: All the indicators point to this place being an active flint mine, except one thing: where are all the miners?
summary: The miners' souls have recently been trapped in small stones. You must free them during the related questthumb|right|Interior
notes: The actual mine entrance can be difficult to find, as it is underground. You can easily get the map marker without seeing the entrance at all. Go north from where the marker appears and into an open-air mine, then turn around to find the entrance to the underground tunnel that leads to the actual mine. The Emberflint mine entrance will be a wooden door in the same underground area where you find the soul crystals that the miners are trapped in.

name: Hightide Hollow
description: an abandoned mine in central Stonefalls, west of Ebonheart containing spiders.
loadtext: The abandoned mine on the coast at Hightide Hollow has been used on and off for centuries as a smugglers' den. Now someone seems to have chased the smugglers out. Who are the new residents?
summary: thumb|right|Interior It has become infested by spiders, which drove out the goblins living in the cave. They are being controlled by an Orc mage named Oodegu. Hazards include: Lava Pools

name: Inner Sea Armature
description: a Dwemer ruin west of Davon's Watch in Stonefalls containing outlaws and Dwarven constructs.
loadtext: What the vanished Dwarven people called this small subterranean site is now lost to history. Modern scholars of the Dwemer call it the "Inner Sea Armature."
summary: The delve consists of circular Dwarven corridors connecting two main chambers, and breaking through into a natural cavern to the south. A Skyshard can be found in the large northernmost chamber. A Tattered Note can be found at a four-way intersection near the entrance to the natural caves. These caves contain the , found laying on the ground near some gears; this is needed for the quest The Precursor. The unique Dwarven Sphere Zozuzetharus can be found in a shallow pool in the center of the natural cavern. During the quest A Mother's Obsession, Irenni Elendis can be found here, imprisoned by the bandits in their pantry. During the quest Long Lost Lore, a Forgotten Tome can be found here if your character is of the Pact.
related_quests: Long Lost Lore; Dwarven Relics of Stonefalls; A Mother's Obsession; The Precursor

name: Mephala's Nest
description: a Daedric ruin in central Stonefalls, just south of Ebonheart containing Shadowsilk goblins and spiders.
loadtext: Ancient Chimer shrines to the Daedric Prince Mephala were referred to in common parlance as "Mephala's Nests." Some of them are remarkably well preserved. Others now host dangerous creatures that have developed a special taste for intrusive scholars.
summary: A Burnt, Mostly Illegible Scrap is located on a bench to the right in the hallway just beyond the entrance. The note implies that the cult of Mephala that previously resided here was wiped out by the Shadowsilk goblins. In the first large room, there are two Shadowsilk Ravagers and witches, and a single giant spider. There are coins on a table underneath the stairs, and a backpack is next to that same table. In this room, you can head up the stairs and go west or you can take the northern path. There's a giant spider at the top of the stairs. Up the northern path is a large rectangular chamber. Two giant spiders, one witch and one ravager patrol the hallway leading up to this room. The east side of this room contains one ravager and a Spider Daedra. Several bookshelves line the walls. A Shadowsilk Witch cheers next to the skyshard and a spider with below average health in the center of the room. name: Sheogorath's Tongue
description: a Daedric ruin in western Stonefalls, north of Kragenmoor, containing bandits.
loadtext: In Morrowind there are many shrines to the "Good Daedra": Azura, Boethiah, and Mephala. Far more rare are shrines to the "Bad Daedra," the Four Corners of the House of Troubles: Mehrunes Dagon, Molag Bal, Malacath … and Sheogorath.
summary: The shrine inside is dedicated to Sheogorath. The Lover can be found on the hill above the delve, to the east. Shivering Shrine is also near the delve. Kennixa's List can be found on the floor in the first hallway. The skyshard and the potions needed for Darkvale Brews can be found in the northern chamber. A chest can be found between two bookshelves in the western part of the same room. There is a chest up on a ledge in the western portion of the first large chamber. It can be accessed by traversing the tunnels and taking the path east when you reach the crossroads in the center of the delve. Assassin Beetles infest the western tunnels. Calls-to-Nature and Dezanu are performing a ritual in the western chamber. A pile of coins can be taken from their altar. Argar's corpse can be found on their pavilion during Ruthless Competition.thumb|right|Western chamber
related_quests: Darkvale Brews; Ruthless Competition (Ebonheart Pact characters only)

name: Softloam Cavern
